Let  

• Distance from the Large Magellanic Cloud to Earth  
 D ≃ 1.6 × 10⁵ light-years (≈ 160 000 ly)  
• Speed of the ship  
 v = 0.999 999 87 c  → β ≡ v/c = 0.999 999 87  

1. Lorentz factor γ  
 γ = 1 / √(1 – β²)  
 β² = (0.999 999 87)² ≃ 0.999 999 74  
 1 – β² ≃ 2.6 × 10⁻⁷  
 γ ≃ 1 / √(2.6 × 10⁻⁷) ≃ 1 / (5.1 × 10⁻⁴) ≃ 2.0 × 10³ ≃ 1.96 × 10³

2. Travel time in Earth’s frame  
 t_E = D / v ≃ 160 000 yr / 0.999 999 87 ≃ 1.6 × 10⁵ yr  

3. Proper time experienced by the astronaut  
 τ = t_E / γ ≃ (1.6 × 10⁵ yr)/(1.96 × 10³) ≃ 8.1 × 10¹ yr ≃ 81 years

The 22-year-old astronaut would therefore age about 81 years during the trip, arriving on Earth at roughly 103 years of age—well within the 150-year life expectancy.

Hence the closest option is

Answer: A
